title: Late-1940s Basie: arrangers and rehearsals
summary: After Pres went into the Army, Basie hired better readers and used arrangements by Mundy, Redman and Fletcher Henderson charts.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, I mean, all through the '40s these tenors were changing. But the band was playing more and more sort of heavily arranged things.

Yeah. Well, the late '40s, I would say, after Pres went in the Army and he didn't come back, then we had to get musicians -- I think Basie got musicians that were more -- they could read better. They would blend in with the section better. Because at that time Jimmy Mundy was writing and -- let's see, who else was writing? Don Redman did some writing.
And then there were arrangements coming out of the band.

Yes, yes. Buck was doing a lot of writing. We played a lot of arrangements of -- Benny Goodman gave Basie quite a few arrangements of Fletcher's. And that incurred more rehearsals, which we weren't used to, either.
